acceptance.given: An invalid-package case is presented for success evaluation.

oracle.expected: The invalid-package case receives a non-success result.
forbidden: Success is accepted for an invalid-package case.
oracle.observable: The terminal result of the evaluated invalid-package case.

acceptance.when: The SM-2 invalid-package selector evaluates the case.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the invalid-package selector against a result marked successful.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Reject a success terminal result when the evaluated case is an invalid package.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Existing terminal categories remain compatible; invalid-package evaluation cannot classify as success.

slice_hint.state_transition: Invalid-package case presented for success evaluation to non-success result recorded.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The invalid-package selector rejects every success result for an invalid-package case.

acceptance.given: A rollback transition is executed for an applicable Consumer, with the Prior Route identity and the Prior Behavior Baseline verdict and diagnostic category captured for each applicable fixture.

oracle.expected: Per-Consumer rollback receipts prove a real invocation of the Prior Route and, for every applicable fixture, equality with the captured Prior Route identity, verdict, and diagnostic category.
forbidden: A configuration-only state change is accepted as rollback reproduction.
A rollback receipt lacks a real Prior Route invocation.
Any applicable fixture has a mismatched Prior Route identity, verdict, or diagnostic category.
oracle.observable: The rollback evaluation emits attributable per-Consumer, per-fixture receipts containing the invoked Prior Route identity and the observed verdict and diagnostic category.

acceptance.then: Rollback succeeds only after every applicable Consumer receipt reproduces the captured Prior Behavior Baseline through the real Prior Route.
acceptance.when: A rollback transition is executed for an applicable Consumer.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Exercise an applicable Consumer rollback where the candidate route is rejected or disabled without invoking the Prior Route; require the rollback check to fail rather than accept the configuration-only outcome.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Add Toolchain rollback evaluation that invokes the Prior Route through each applicable real Consumer and compares the invoked route identity, verdict, and diagnostic category against the captured Prior Behavior Baseline for every applicable fixture; reject configuration-only, rejection-only, missing-call, or mismatched reproduction.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Restore the prior Toolchain replay behavior without persistent-state or schema migration; existing receipts remain compatible, while rollback receipts lacking real Prior Route invocation or baseline equality remain non-successful.

slice_hint.state_transition: Rollback scheduled for an applicable Consumer with a captured Prior Behavior Baseline -> real Prior Route invocation for each applicable fixture -> per-fixture identity/verdict/diagnostic comparison -> reproduced rollback receipt or failed rollback.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Every applicable Consumer has a rollback receipt for every applicable fixture that proves real Prior Route invocation and exact reproduction of the captured Prior Route identity, verdict, and diagnostic category; otherwise rollback is unsuccessful.

acceptance.given: Toolchain replay entry point, capability descriptor, and existing replay regression selector are available; closure validation has not been assumed to pass.

oracle.expected: Closure validation records every result-affecting executable, data artifact, policy, configuration value, and environment representation, and rejects a closure narrowed by Probe reachability.
forbidden: A result-affecting semantic dependency is omitted.
Probe reachability defines or narrows the Semantic Dependency closure.
oracle.observable: The replay regression selector evaluates the emitted semantic-dependency closure and an omission case.

acceptance.then: The closure is exhaustive across the five mandatory categories and fails closed when Probe reachability is used to omit a member.
acceptance.when: Validator Capability or Current Snapshot dependencies are established or validated.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Use the existing replay regression selector to verify that a closure omitting a result-affecting member because it is not Probe-reachable is rejected.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Extend repository-owned replay validation so Semantic Dependency closure includes every result-affecting executable, data artifact, policy, configuration value, and environment representation; Probe reachability cannot define or narrow it.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing replay receipt compatibility while rejecting incomplete or Probe-reachability-narrowed closures.

slice_hint.state_transition: From a potentially incomplete dependency set to a five-category exhaustive closure that fails closed on reachability-based omission.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Closure validation succeeds only when all five categories cover every result-affecting dependency and Probe reachability has not narrowed the closure.

acceptance.given: A defined six-case Stable/Candidate replay matrix and its case-execution evidence are supplied to the Toolchain replay path.

oracle.expected: For every Matrix Case, verification establishes a case-unique fixture identity or state-transition identity, a frozen case expectation, one Stable execution, one Candidate execution, and two separately attributable observations; no such identity or observation is reused as another case's owned context.
forbidden: Any two Matrix Cases share a fixture or state-transition identity.
Any Matrix Case lacks its frozen expectation, Stable execution, Candidate execution, or separate observations.
oracle.observable: The S2 matrix verification emits per-case structural evidence binding the case ID to its owned fixture/state-transition identity, frozen expectation, Stable and Candidate execution records, and separate observation records.

acceptance.then: The matrix is accepted only when every case independently satisfies the complete ownership tuple.
acceptance.when: The authored S2 runtime matrix selector evaluates the replay evidence.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the S2 selector after assigning two Matrix Cases the same fixture or state-transition identity; observe structural rejection.
Run the S2 selector after removing one Matrix Case's frozen expectation; observe structural rejection.
Run the S2 selector after omitting one subject execution or one separately attributable observation from a Matrix Case; observe aggregate rejection.

affected_subjects: Matrix Case fixture or state-transition ownership
slice_hint.behavior_change: Require the Toolchain matrix replay path to reject a Matrix Case unless it owns a fixture or state transition distinct from every other case and binds its frozen expectation, both Stable/Candidate executions, and separate observations.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve the existing replay receipt contract and non-authorizing lifecycle semantics; remove only the added ownership validation if rollback is required.

slice_hint.state_transition: A defined or evaluated Matrix Case moves from unverified case metadata to independently owned fixture/state-transition evidence with frozen expectation, two subject executions, and separate observations.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The S2 selector passes only if all six Matrix Cases have pairwise distinct owned fixture-or-state-transition contexts and each case has its own frozen expectation, Stable execution, Candidate execution, and separate observations; otherwise the aggregate is unsuccessful.
